clips.send: Stave 1, Christmas Eve. “Bah!” said Scrooge, “Humbug!” He snaps at his cheerful nephew Fred and refuses to give a penny to men collecting for the poor.
clips.text: Stave 1 · Christmas Eve. “Bah!” said Scrooge, “Humbug!” He snaps at his cheerful nephew Fred and refuses to give a penny to men collecting for the poor.

clips.send: Stave 2, Christmas Past. “The happiness he gives, is quite as great as if it cost a fortune.” Watching his kind old boss Fezziwig’s party, Scrooge praises generosity — and thinks of his own clerk.

clips.send: Stave 4, Christmas Yet to Come. “I am not the man I was.” Shown a lonely, unmourned death, Scrooge begs for a chance to change.
clips.text: Stave 4 · Christmas Yet to Come. “I am not the man I was.” Shown a lonely, unmourned death, Scrooge begs for a chance to change.

clips.send: Stave 1, The miser. “Oh! But he was a tight-fisted hand at the grindstone, Scrooge! a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner!” The narrator tells us directly what Scrooge is like — a pile-up of greedy verbs.
clips.text: Stave 1 · The miser. “Oh! But he was a tight-fisted hand at the grindstone, Scrooge! a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner!” The narrator tells us directly what Scrooge is like — a pile-up of greedy verbs.

clips.send: Stave 3, Christmas Present. “Spirit,” said Scrooge, with an interest he had never felt before, “tell me if Tiny Tim will live.” He sees his clerk Bob Cratchit’s poor family and their sick boy — and begins to care.
clips.text: Stave 3 · Christmas Present. “Spirit,” said Scrooge, with an interest he had never felt before, “tell me if Tiny Tim will live.” He sees his clerk Bob Cratchit’s poor family and their sick boy — and begins to care.

clips.send: Stave 5, Christmas morning. “I am as light as a feather, I am as happy as an angel, I am as merry as a school-boy.” He sends the Cratchits a prize turkey, raises Bob’s salary and becomes “as good a man as the good old city knew”.

clips.send: Stave 1, Marley’s ghost. “I wear the chain I forged in life.” His dead partner warns him: a greedy life becomes a heavy chain. Scrooge is frightened, but not yet changed.

clips.send: 第一章 · 守财奴。“唉，斯克鲁奇真是个一毛不拔的人！一个榨取、拧夺、攫取、刮削、紧抓不放、贪得无厌的老罪人！” 叙述者直接告诉我们斯克鲁奇是什么样的人——一连串表示贪婪的词。
clips.text: 第一章 · 守财奴. “唉，斯克鲁奇真是个一毛不拔的人！一个榨取、拧夺、攫取、刮削、紧抓不放、贪得无厌的老罪人！” 叙述者直接告诉我们斯克鲁奇是什么样的人——一连串表示贪婪的词。

clips.send: 第四章 · 未来之灵。“我已经不是从前的我了。” 看到自己孤独死去、无人哀悼的结局，斯克鲁奇恳求一次改变的机会。
clips.text: 第四章 · 未来之灵. “我已经不是从前的我了。” 看到自己孤独死去、无人哀悼的结局，斯克鲁奇恳求一次改变的机会。

clips.send: 第一章 · 马利的鬼魂。“我戴着的是我生前亲手打造的锁链。” 他死去的合伙人警告他：贪婪的一生会变成沉重的锁链。斯克鲁奇吓坏了，但还没有改变。

clips.send: 第二章 · 过去之灵。“他给人的快乐，就像花了一大笔钱那样珍贵。” 看着善良的老东家费兹威格举办舞会，斯克鲁奇称赞起慷慨来——还想到了自己的伙计。

clips.send: 第一章 · 平安夜。“哼！”斯克鲁奇说，“胡扯！” 他冲着快乐的外甥弗雷德发火，还拒绝给为穷人募捐的人一分钱。
clips.text: 第一章 · 平安夜. “哼！”斯克鲁奇说，“胡扯！” 他冲着快乐的外甥弗雷德发火，还拒绝给为穷人募捐的人一分钱。

clips.send: 第三章 · 现在之灵。“精灵，”斯克鲁奇带着从未有过的关切问道，“告诉我，小蒂姆能活下去吗？” 他看到伙计鲍勃·克拉奇特一家的贫困和生病的儿子——开始关心别人了。
clips.text: 第三章 · 现在之灵. “精灵，”斯克鲁奇带着从未有过的关切问道，“告诉我，小蒂姆能活下去吗？” 他看到伙计鲍勃·克拉奇特一家的贫困和生病的儿子——开始关心别人了。

clips.send: 第五章 · 圣诞节早晨。“我轻得像一根羽毛，快乐得像一个天使，高兴得像一个小学生。” 他给克拉奇特家送去一只得奖的大火鸡，给鲍勃涨了工资，成了“这座古老城市里最好的人”。
